paths.description: Homepage and consent entry state; represents the main news front, global navigation, and first-visit experience.
World section listing; represents section/index templates. Other section pages sharing this template were not duplicated.
Long-form lifestyle article; represents article/content templates, reading, metadata, embedded forms, and mobile reflow.
Newsletter listing; represents subscription discovery and newsletter entry flows.

A representative missing/search URL to assess HTTP failure recovery. The Guardian delegates site search to Google, so this path represents the 404 template rather than a supported search-results template.
Guardian account sign-in entry; represents authentication and account continuation.

findings.summary: The main Guardian site is fixed to a light color scheme.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in composition and colours to the default capture; the DOM reports html color-scheme: light and body background rgb(255,255,255).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light dark support in the head and root, then theme surfaces and browser UI from prefers-color-scheme using color-scheme and semantic color tokens.

findings.summary: Page and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion/source probe found no view-transition rules, and navigation is conventional full-document replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance eligible same-origin navigation with cross-document View Transitions, preserving an instant fallback and disabling non-essential motion under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long article chrome provides no visible scroll progress or scroll-state response.
findings.evidence: The long article template has many sections, while DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state container behaviour and the captured header is static.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained article progress affordance using declarative scroll-driven styling, with reduced-motion treatment.

findings.summary: A full-viewport consent-or-pay dialog obscures all content on first visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile first-load screenshots show the article/front content dimmed and inaccessible behind a fixed aria-modal dialog covering the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking first-load wall with a proportionate consent surface that allows an equally prominent privacy-preserving continuation and keeps core journalism readable.

findings.summary: Rich overlays use custom role=dialog divs rather than native dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: Article DOM inspection found gallery overlays as DIV role=dialog, while the consent system is an iframe wrapped by a custom aria-modal DIV.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native dialog for modal flows, with labelled headings, focus return, Escape handling, and platform close semantics; use popover for transient non-modal UI.

findings.summary: The primary reading journey cannot continue without accepting personalised advertising or purchasing Ad-Lite.
findings.evidence: The article mobile capture remains blocked by the consent-or-pay dialog; the only primary actions are “Accept all” and “Reject all and subscribe”.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a direct, equally prominent “Reject optional cookies and continue” path and move subscription promotion into a separate, non-blocking choice.

findings.summary: Mobile synthetic load performance misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 5.9s, LCP 8.8s, TTI 9.3s and performance 0.60; the raw-CDP trace under a lighter desktop profile measured LCP 2.10s, showing condition sensitivity but confirming mobile risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the mobile LCP element, prioritise its discovery, reduce document/consent latency, defer non-critical work, and verify against mobile Lighthouse and field CWV.

findings.summary: Critical delivery includes avoidable latency, cache and font/image inefficiencies.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 820ms redirect savings, 153KiB cache-lifetime savings, font-display issues and 149KiB image savings; HAR records 108 requests and 1.14MB transferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the root-to-edition redirect where possible, tighten cache lifetimes, use font-display with stable fallbacks, and correctly prioritise only the LCP image.

findings.summary: The initial load ships substantial unused, duplicated and legacy JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 187KiB unused JS, 24KiB duplicated JS and 28KiB legacy JS; HAR records 44 script requests and 412,622 transferred script bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage and long-animation-frame attribution to remove duplicate modules, stop sending legacy code to modern browsers, and conditionally load commercial/consent features.

findings.summary: Some controls and composite widgets have incomplete accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails button-name and aria-required-children; the direct probe counted one unnamed button.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every button an accessible name and repair required child roles using native elements where possible; retest the accessibility tree and keyboard flow.

findings.summary: List and accessibility-tree structure is malformed in parts of the homepage.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the list audit and agent accessibility-tree audit, although the direct focus probe shows a visible 3px blue focus treatment on sampled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure lists contain only valid list children, preserve logical landmark/heading order, and verify the repaired accessibility tree with assistive technology.

findings.summary: Most homepage images omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 98 of 100 images without width/height attributes. Although observed CLS was low in this run, the markup leaves stability dependent on CSS and timing.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height (or an equivalent intrinsic aspect ratio) from image metadata for every content image.

findings.summary: Homepage canonical and robots/sitemap signals are inconsistent for automated audits.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails canonical and robots.txt validity; the requested /sitemap.xml returns 404 while robots points to HTTP news/video sitemap URLs. The rendered final URL is /uk but canonical is the root.
findings.suggestedFix: Align edition canonical policy with the final URL, serve valid sitemap discovery endpoints over HTTPS, and keep robots syntax consumable by common validators.

findings.summary: CSP and cookie settings leave avoidable browser-enforced security gaps.
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS and nosniff but CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. Cookie inspection found two first-party cookies without Secure and all seven set SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Move toward nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval, mark all cookies Secure, and use Lax/Strict unless a documented cross-site use requires None.

findings.summary: The first-visit page makes a broad analytics and consent-related request footprint before a choice.
findings.evidence: HAR records 105 cross-origin requests by origin classification and 968KB, including 12 Sourcepoint and 10 Ophan requests; aborted Ophan URLs include attention, performance, experiments and consent-view events.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise pre-consent telemetry to essential events, batch allowed analytics after choice, and document each cross-origin processor and retention purpose.

findings.summary: The consent choice uses asymmetric accept-or-pay framing.
findings.evidence: The modal offers “Accept all” versus “Reject all and subscribe” with no equally prominent free rejection path, coupling privacy refusal to a £5/month purchase.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate consent from subscription, offer symmetric accept/reject controls, and make optional processing off by default without confirmshaming or forced continuity.

findings.summary: The embedded newsletter email field omits an autocomplete token.
findings.evidence: Article form inspection found type=email and a visible label but autocomplete is empty; the account sign-in email field correctly uses autocomplete=email.
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete=email to newsletter email fields and preserve the existing explicit label and input type.

findings.summary: Image delivery does not consistently use responsive source selection or modern formats.
findings.evidence: The image probe reports 89 of 100 images without srcset, 100 legacy-format URLs, 14 below-fold images not lazy-loaded and two oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP through picture or content negotiation, emit srcset/sizes from known renditions, and lazy-load below-fold imagery while keeping the LCP image eager.

findings.summary: Background analytics and experiment traffic starts on the blocked first-visit state.
findings.evidence: HAR captures repeated Ophan attention, performance, experiment and component events while the consent wall is still the only usable surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-essential analytics until consent and idle time, coalesce events, and stop session-wide attention updates when the page is obscured or backgrounded.

findings.summary: Consent and font resources consume a disproportionate share of the first-load budget.
findings.evidence: Of 1.14MB transferred, fonts account for 252KB and Sourcepoint consent resources 202KB; the single Notice script is 94.9KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset and consolidate fonts, cache them aggressively, and reduce/defer consent-vendor code so the first visit prioritises journalism.

taskList.title: Replace the consent-or-pay wall with symmetric, non-blocking privacy choices
Fix mobile LCP and first-load critical delivery
Repair button, list and accessibility-tree semantics
Modernise responsive image delivery and intrinsic sizing
Reduce pre-consent analytics, consent code and font overhead
Align canonical, robots and sitemap signals
Use native overlay primitives and add newsletter autocomplete
Progressively enhance route and article navigation cues
